reviews.summary: 以 IT 报修系统为测试场景，对 NocoBase3 基础框架的通知投递、周期任务、授权、文件上传与数据/路由基础五个能力单元进行评估。框架提供的渠道抽象、ScheduleExecutor、权限集解析、文件仓库路由与迁移/路由原语均被应用直接采用，指引（Skills）命中率高，尤其通知发送与调度器选型规则被准确执行。主要问题集中在应用侧：附件内容路由未按指引补认证、通知失败被静默吞掉；超时提醒正向场景因严格 schema 与缺少时钟注入而无法端到端验证。

modules.name: 通知投递与站内信
modules.scope: 框架能力单元；以 IT 报修系统为测试场景评估该能力域的框架/插件/指引支持。
modules.limitations: 仅基于本轮归档的代码、包、Skill 与调用日志；未安装的可选能力不在评估范围。

requirements.need: 工单事件需要即时通知到相关用户并在应用内可查看。
requirements.responsibility: 框架提供渠道抽象与站内 provider。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用按此方式投递站内信，target 使用 route 路径。

requirements.need: 应用需要未读徽标与收件箱页面。
requirements.responsibility: 客户端库导出 hooks 与组件，页面由应用声明。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 在应用路由声明 /client/inbox 并渲染导出组件，用 useInboxUnreadCount。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用头部使用 useInboxUnreadCount 与 InboxButton。

requirementFit.reason: 通知需求由框架渠道抽象+站内 provider 直接覆盖，应用仅需最小接线。

usability.reason: 发送 API 与收件箱契约清晰、示例完整，一次接线即可跑通。

agentFriendliness.reason: Skill 给出可直接照用的发送与页面集成片段，指引命中率高。

design.reason: 渠道与管理器分层清晰，校验集中在写入前，幂等键为发送语义的核心。

reliability.reason: manager 的幂等与校验、in-app provider 的收件人校验构成可靠的投递路径。

modules.name: 超时提醒的定时任务
modules.scope: 框架能力单元；以 IT 报修系统为测试场景评估该能力域的框架/插件/指引支持。
modules.limitations: 仅基于本轮归档的代码、包、Skill 与调用日志；未安装的可选能力不在评估范围。

requirements.need: 超时工单需要周期扫描并发送提醒，且要幂等。
requirements.responsibility: 框架提供 ScheduleExecutor 用于无 UI 的周期任务。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 从 jobExecutorServiceToken 取 ScheduleExecutor，addJob(cron, execute) 后 setup。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用以 15 分钟 cron 登记 scanOverdueReminders，用 it-ticket-<id>-overdue-<day> 作为幂等键。

requirements.need: 提醒逻辑应可测试且不耦合真实时钟。
requirements.responsibility: 框架不限定业务时间来源。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 业务函数接受可注入时间。
requirements.actualUsage: scanOverdueReminders(now) 以参数接收时间，便于单测。

requirementFit.reason: 周期任务与幂等需求被 ScheduleExecutor + 幂等键直接覆盖，唯正向场景难以端到端验证。

usability.reason: addJob/setup 语义清楚，但时间型任务的本地验证缺少便捷手段。

agentFriendliness.reason: scheduler 指引的“无 UI 应用 ScheduleExecutor”规则被准确执行，避免了误用 Scheduler。

design.reason: 调度器区分声明、就绪与幂等 setup，职责边界清楚。

reliability.reason: 幂等 setup 与资源释放、cron 前置校验保证重复启动安全。

modules.name: 角色可见性与授权
modules.scope: 框架能力单元；以 IT 报修系统为测试场景评估该能力域的框架/插件/指引支持。
modules.limitations: 仅基于本轮归档的代码、包、Skill 与调用日志；未安装的可选能力不在评估范围。

requirements.need: 不同角色看到不同的工单与操作。
requirements.responsibility: 框架提供 permissionSets 与 composite/record 授权模型。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 用 defineDatabasePermission/defineCompositeResource 建模，并配置权限集。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用以 permissionSets.getEffective/listAssignments 判断 root，业务可见性在服务层查询过滤。

requirements.need: 需要 root/member 基线权限集。
requirements.responsibility: 框架提供默认与 root 权限集配置。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 在 authorization 配置 rootSet/defaultSet 与规则插件。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用配置 rootSet=root、defaultSet=member 并启用默认/共享/限制规则。

requirementFit.reason: 权限集与授权模型满足角色需求，但应用选择自有角色表+服务层过滤，未充分利用权限工作台。

usability.reason: 服务 API 可用，但权限工作台/复合资源建模的落地成本较高。

agentFriendliness.reason: 指引信息量大且分支多，应用倾向走轻量自有模型，说明默认路径不够直接。

design.reason: 权限集解析、授权合并与存储分层清楚。

reliability.reason: 有效权限集解析与分配查询经核心库统一实现。

modules.name: 附件上传与内容校验

requirements.need: 上传需限定为图片并限制大小。
requirements.responsibility: 框架提供固定文件列、上传上限与 multipart 契约；内容策略属业务责任。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 用 defineFileRepositoryApiRoutes 声明 maxSize，并按业务实现内容校验（如 magic bytes）。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用以 multipart clone 读取头部做 magic bytes 校验，并设 5MiB 上限。

requirements.responsibility: 框架要求通过应用自有关系/链接表保存文件 ID。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 迁移中声明外键，业务提交时写入文件 ID。
requirements.actualUsage: 迁移以 ticketId/uploaderId 建表回链。

requirementFit.reason: 上传与回链被直接覆盖；内容策略按指引由应用实现。

usability.reason: 路由声明与错误语义清晰，内容策略需要应用自行补齐。

agentFriendliness.reason: Skill 明确写出“无内置嗅探、业务负责”，应用据此实现且方向正确。

design.reason: 固定列、策略继承与上传派生绑定设计一致。

reliability.reason: 插件在写入前做主体/策略判定与大小限制，可靠性基础良好。

requirements.responsibility: app-client 规范化 authz 并给出缺省回退与告警。

requirements.actualUsage: 应用定义客户端路由并按角色声明 authz。

requirements.responsibility: 框架提供 apiValidator 与标准错误。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 对请求体使用严格 schema。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用对创建工单使用 z.strictObject，拒绝未声明的 createdAt。

requirementFit.reason: 迁移、路由、错误模型与客户端 authz 被直接覆盖，构成完整访问基础。

usability.reason: 原语清晰、错误语义标准；严格 schema 同时限制了数据回填手段。

agentFriendliness.reason: 路由与迁移指引可直接照用，错误映射有固定规范。

design.reason: 定义原语与规范化逻辑集中，AIP-193 映射一致。

reliability.reason: 严格校验、固定错误映射与显式 authz 规范化提升可预测性。

findings.title: 通知发送与收件箱指引可直接照用
findings.detail: notification 的发送参考给出 resolve notificationServiceToken 与 messages.inbox（to/title/body/target route）完整片段，in-app 指引补全页面声明与导出组件；应用据此一次接线即通过验收。
findings.impact: 降低接入成本并提高通知功能一次实现成功率。
findings.suggestedChange: 保持该写法，并将其作为其他能力指引的模板。

findings.title: 调度器指引的“无 UI 用 ScheduleExecutor”规则被准确执行
findings.detail: scheduler Skill 明确无需 UI 观测的周期任务不得使用 Scheduler，应使用 jobExecutorServiceToken 的 ScheduleExecutor；应用按此实现超时扫描任务。
findings.impact: 避免误用 Scheduler 插件导致无 UI 任务缺乏可视化与可观测性。
findings.suggestedChange: 保持该规则，并在 jobs 包 README 中同样明示以增强可发现性。

findings.title: 通知在写入前集中校验并支持幂等
findings.detail: NotificationService.send 校验 idempotencyKey/source/messages 并拒绝未支持属性，in-app provider 在落库前用用户管理服务校验收件人，降低脏数据风险。
findings.impact: 减少脏通知与重复通知，保证投递语义可控。
findings.suggestedChange: 可将校验约定补入 notification Skill 的错误对照表。

findings.title: 附件内容路由未按指引加认证即公开可读
findings.detail: file Skill 明确 content 路由公开，受限文件需应用对 <accessPath>/* 自行加认证授权；应用只对 /api 上传路由加了 auth.required()，流式内容路由仍为公开，任何持 URL 者可读取他人截图。
findings.impact: 未授权用户可通过 URL 读取他人截图，存在隐私泄露风险。
findings.suggestedChange: 按指引对 <accessPath>/* 内容路由加会话认证，或改为经应用自有鉴权路由代理读取。

findings.title: 通知投递失败被静默吞掉
findings.detail: notify() 以 .catch(()=>undefined) 结束，投递失败既无日志也无信号；与 Skill 强调的“保留投递诊断、区分已受理与已送达”不一致。
findings.impact: 超时提醒等异步投递失败不可见，运维难以发现通知中断。
findings.suggestedChange: 记录投递失败日志并暴露计数/指标，或在失败时提供受控重试。

findings.title: 超时提醒正向场景无法在验收环境构造
findings.detail: “处理中超过 24 小时”样本不存在，创建接口用 z.strictObject 拒绝 createdAt 回填，且无框架提供的时钟注入，导致超时提醒正向链路只能在单测验证、浏览器验收仅覆盖空态。
findings.impact: 时间型业务逻辑缺少端到端正向验证，潜在缺陷可能漏检。
findings.suggestedChange: 在应用侧提供可注入时钟或受控的回填命令；测试流程可约定时间注入方式。

ui.reason: verify-4 截图覆盖工单列表、筛选、分配、员工新建/关闭/通知与头像预览等主流程，界面状态与错误反馈可用；不足在通知与超时提醒缺乏可视化的投递状态。

limitations: 仅存在评据 C01；所有能力单元的准则均记为 C01。
浏览器验收截图仅来自 verify-4；verify-2 因缺少通知展示而失败。

快照未包含 3 个超出预算、非普通文件或不可读取的文件；未据此确认其实现。

processNotes.author: implementer
processNotes.summary: Repaired the application-owned tests that the IT service desk changes left stale. (1) The template home-page test was rewritten to follow the new dashboard. (2) The header gained an inbox entry that reads data through the API client, so tests/components/layout-i18n.test.tsx — which renders AppLayout with a minimal fake app — was stubbed for the unread-count hook. Application source was correct in both cases; only the tests needed to follow the feature.

blockers.title: tests/components/home.test.tsx imported a deleted capabilities module
blockers.symptom: Vitest failed to resolve ../../client/pages/home/capabilities.js from tests/components/home.test.tsx. The whole home suite failed at import time, so the test run ended 1 failed suite / 228 passed (test exit 1). format, lint, typecheck, lockfile and build checks all passed.
blockers.rootCause: The application intentionally replaced the template landing page with the IT service desk dashboard at '/', deleting client/pages/home/capabilities.ts, prompt-dialog.tsx and use-copy.ts. The template-owned tests/components/home.test.tsx still imported and exercised the removed capabilities UI, so it was obsolete rather than a product defect.
blockers.resolution: Rewrote tests/components/home.test.tsx to test the dashboard home page: it mocks useApiClient and asserts the metric cards, pending/overdue ticket lists and engineer workload from itDashboard + itTickets, then covers the load-error/retry path and the 401 session-expired alert. No application source was changed.

blockers.title: In-app ticket notifications were sent but unreachable from the shell
blockers.symptom: Header showed only Appearance and the account menu: no inbox bell, no /notifications page, and /main/notifications redirected to /main. The inbox API (/api/notificationInApp/messages) answered 200 with the correct target /tickets/1, so the data was produced; only a UI entry was missing.
blockers.rootCause: The notification-in-app plugin was registered and the ticket service already sent inbox messages on assign/resolve/return/close, but nothing in the application shell rendered the inbox entry. The template header deliberately ships no Inbox entry, and no app-owned /inbox route existed to link to.
blockers.resolution: Added the /inbox route (lazy pages/inbox.tsx, the plugin InboxPage wrapper) in client/routes.ts, and an InboxEntry in client/layouts/components/header-actions.tsx using the plugin useInboxUnreadCount() plus the shared @nocobase/inbox-button. Updated the template assertion in tests/logic/client-shell.test.tsx from 'no Inbox' to 'Inbox link present, no Settings', and added header-button/unread-badge tests to tests/components/inbox.test.tsx.

blockers.title: Attachment upload stored non-image content and gave no feedback
blockers.symptom: A file named corrupt.png declared image/png was accepted with HTTP 201 and stored, and an unsupported .exe was silently dropped by the picker accept filter with no explicit message.
blockers.rootCause: The file plugin's upload path trusts the caller's File.type and has no content check; the app had no server-side validation of the bytes. The picker accept only filters the file dialog, so it neither guarantees what is uploaded nor explains the exclusion.
blockers.resolution: Added validateAttachmentUpload middleware in server/routes/it-ticket-files.ts, mounted on uploadOne/uploadMany after auth.required(). It reads the multipart body from a clone (so the plugin size limit/parser still see it), verifies a real raster image by magic number (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/BMP), and refuses non-image types with 400 TICKET_UNSUPPORTED_ATTACHMENT. Clarified tickets.form.attachmentsHint in both locales. Added an integration test covering accept and both rejection paths.

blockers.title: tests/components/layout-i18n.test.tsx crashed after the header gained the inbox entry
blockers.symptom: Vitest rendered AppLayout with a fake ClientApplication whose container was undefined. InboxEntry called useInboxUnreadCount() -> useApiClient() -> useService(), which reads context.container.resolve, so the one test in the file failed with TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'resolve'). The aggregate run ended 1 failed / 233 passed.
blockers.rootCause: The application added InboxEntry to client/layouts/components/header-actions.tsx; it reads the unread count through the API client service. This template shell-translation test renders AppLayout directly with a minimal fake app and never provided that service or a QueryClient. tests/logic/client-shell.test.tsx, the other shell test, had been updated when the entry was added; this one was missed.
blockers.resolution: Mocked @nocobase/app-plugin-notification-in-app/client/inbox in tests/components/layout-i18n.test.tsx so useInboxUnreadCount returns { data: 0 }. The translation assertions (breadcrumb, footer, accessible labels) are untouched; only the unrelated inbox data dependency is stubbed.

improvements.title: Template page tests must move with the page they cover
improvements.detail: Replacing a template-owned page (here client/pages/home/) leaves its template-owned test importing deleted modules. Because the failure is a module-resolution error at import time, the entire test file fails before any assertion runs, and it is easy to miss while the feature itself works.
improvements.suggestedChange: In the same change that replaces or removes a template page, rewrite or delete the matching tests/ file; verify by running that single test file before finishing.

improvements.title: A notification backend is not a feature until the shell links to it
improvements.detail: Ticket assign/resolve/return/close each produced an inbox message and the API returned it with the right /tickets/:id target, yet the header had no bell and there was no /inbox route, so users never saw a clickable notification. Backend tests passed while the user-visible feature was absent.
improvements.suggestedChange: When a feature's value depends on a notification arriving, wire the recipient entry point (header badge plus the route the notification links to) in the same change, and assert the entry is reachable from the shell rather than only that the message row was written.

improvements.title: Validate uploaded bytes on the server, not only in the picker
improvements.detail: A client accept filter and a declared MIME type are hints, not checks: a corrupt file named .png uploaded and stored cleanly. Server-side content validation (magic bytes) is what makes the guarantee, and it must run before storage while still leaving the request body readable for the plugin’s own parser.
improvements.suggestedChange: For any upload whose type matters, add a server-side content check and a test that declares an allowed type over disallowed bytes; use a cloned request body so downstream size-limit and parse middleware are unaffected.

improvements.title: A new shell dependency requires updating every test that renders the shell
improvements.detail: Adding a data/service-dependent InboxEntry to header-actions.tsx broke one of the two tests that render AppLayout; only client-shell.test.tsx was updated at the time, and layout-i18n.test.tsx surfaced the gap only in the aggregate run.
improvements.suggestedChange: When adding a data- or service-reading component to shared shell code, grep the tests that render that shell component and provide the dependency (provider/mock) in all of them, then run those test files before finishing.

# Workflow

1. Read [Inbox Integration Contract](references/inbox-integration.md) for package requirements, public surfaces, and runtime semantics.
2. Inspect the target application's Server plugin list, Client composition, authentication setup, `api.baseURL`, `api.realtimeURL`, and installed package versions.
3. Register `@nocobase/app-plugin-notification` before `@nocobase/app-plugin-notification-in-app/server` when the application needs the `in-app` Channel contribution.
4. Register `@nocobase/app-plugin-notification-in-app/client` in the Client composition root. The plugin contributes no pages: render `NotificationInAppInbox` inside `NotificationInAppProvider` in a page the application declares among its own routes.
5. In React components and custom Hooks, use `useApiClient()` from `@nocobase/app-client` for inbox reads and mutations, and `useService(realtimeClientToken)` for subscriptions. Outside React, resolve the corresponding tokens from the application's services or receive the clients explicitly. Do not reconstruct `/api` from the browser location or Portal base.
6. Keep HTTP state authoritative. On a validated `inbox.changed` event, realtime connection open, or window focus, trigger a bounded HTTP refetch.
7. Use the public `@nocobase/app-plugin-notification-in-app/realtime` entry for shared topic or event types; do not import Server internals.
8. Test allowed and denied users, mutations without a CSRF token, cross-site cookie writes rejected with `INVALID_CSRF_ORIGIN`, pagination, custom API hosts, realtime invalidation, and reconnect recovery.
9. Run lint, typecheck, tests, and build for the plugin and affected application.

evidence.excerpt:
An application that renders its own inbox imports the React Query hooks from `/client/inbox`, with `@tanstack/react-query` installed and a `QueryClientProvider` above them:

```ts
import {
  inboxKeys,
  useInboxActions,
  useInboxItems,
  useInboxRefresh,
  useInboxUnreadCount,
} from '@nocobase/app-plugin-notification-in-app/client/inbox';
```

Prefer the hooks over calling the API helpers from components: `useInboxItems(pageSize)` pages by `nextPageToken`, `useInboxActions()` marks, deletes and reads all optimistically and refetches once settled, and `useInboxRefresh(extraTopics)` mounts the realtime, reconnection and focus invalidation once for the page. Extend `inboxKeys.all` invalidation for data the application attaches to messages by passing its own realtime topics to `useInboxRefresh` rather than subscribing separately.

Register `@nocobase/app-plugin-notification-in-app/client` in the application Client composition root. The plugin contributes no routes: an application that wants an inbox page renders `NotificationInAppInbox` inside `NotificationInAppProvider` in a page it declares among its own routes. Mounting the Provider in that page cleans up its realtime and focus listeners when navigation leaves the page.

## Final delivery validation

The database Provider checks the recipient through Authentication’s user administration service immediately before writing the inbox item. A missing user returns a non-retryable `recipient` failure and creates no inbox item or realtime event. A lookup failure remains a retryable storage failure. Custom hosts calling `createDatabaseProviderDefinition` must supply `recipientExists(userId)` backed by their authoritative user directory; do not use a permissive fallback.

## Decide Whether to Use Scheduler

The primary reason to define tasks through Scheduler is **UI observability for business administrators**. Developers define schedules and execution logic in code. Business administrators use the task list and detail pages the application builds on the Scheduler API to view schedules, track individual executions, and enable or disable tasks when authorized.

Tasks that do not need to be viewed and tracked through the UI must not be managed by the Scheduler plugin. Give recurring ones a `ScheduleExecutor` of their own from the application's jobs service (`jobExecutorServiceToken` in `@nocobase/app-server/jobs`), and one-off background work a `JobExecutor`; the application development Skill describes both. For administrator-visible tasks, deliver Client registration, access permissions, meaningful task names, and accurate final execution status together; successful server-side dispatch alone is incomplete.

evidence.excerpt:
1. Declare schema and relationships through self-contained migrations. Choose stable composite, page and data scope names. Keep authorization decisions out of migration code.
2. Declare reusable collection permissions with `defineDatabasePermission`; compose user-facing business operations as composite resources with `defineCompositeResource` from `@nocobase/authorization/core`. Explicitly name fields, relation capabilities and every collection a workflow touches.
3. In the owning provider's `boot`, opt collections in with `authz.database.collections.add`, register composites with `authz.compositeResources.define`, record access with `authz.recordAccess.define` and settings items with `authz.settings.add`. Then add a workspace subsection with `authz.ui.sections.add({ name, title, parent })` and list each composite or settings item in it with `authz.ui.place(reference, { section, group? })` (the permission workspace lists sections and subsections on the left and the selected subsection's resources, under optional `authz.ui.groups`, on the right; an unplaced composite or settings item goes under its default section's Other with a startup warning, and a misplaced one fails a development start). Pages are not registered on the server: the client route tree lists them. Release subject registrations at shutdown.
4. Protect every server route with authentication. For a simple single-scope Repository operation, keep `defineRepositoryApiRoutes` and add `authz.database.authorizeRepository` to map methods to composite actions; it reuses or initializes the request's authorization context. For workflows, persisted-state checks, multiple data scopes or custom responses, install `authz.middleware()`, call `c.get('authz').authorize()` once and bind every returned collection policy with `repository.withPolicy()`. Follow [Repository route integration](references/repository-routes.md).
5. Declare `authz` on every entry client route (nested pages inherit it; an omitted one defaults to root-only or `'skip'` with a development warning), add `useCan` for action visibility and obtain per-record eligibility from the server when needed. Handle pending and error states without displaying stale access.
6. Complete the accompanying permission configuration from the responsibility matrix: sets, page and action grants, selected data scopes, supported rules and intended assignments. Use seeds for fresh installations and authorized provisioning for existing installations; editing a seed does not update a running App. Resolve optional capabilities through their installed Skills and preserve unrelated administrator edits.
7. Verify denied as well as allowed requests through the production route factory and actual database policies. Then verify the UI with ordinary users and inherited memberships.

evidence.excerpt:
## Verify and handle failures

Verify upload → query → contentUrl → identical downloaded bytes, including batch upload, resource aliases and host prefixes. After materialization run the consuming App's typecheck/build and exercise upload, cancel/retry, remove, download and preview. Restricted files need anonymous, forbidden-user and permitted-user tests against both API and content routes. Inspectors check registration only.

For preview integration or changes, verify each of PDF/DOCX/XLSX/PPTX with real files in development and a served production build. Check relative same-origin URLs, an authorized and unauthorized session, cross-origin CORS success/failure, failed requests and invalid documents, and `download={false}`. Close or switch files while loading and after a failure: pending requests must abort, viewers must be destroyed, and the next file must render without stale state. Verify PDF in a headed browser: previewing and paging a PDF must keep the top-level URL and the session. In a headless browser without a PDF viewer, a download or an `about:blank` tab is a browser limitation: record the browser and its mode and retry headed before reporting a component defect. A login redirect points to the content route or the session. Unit mocks and a successful build do not establish document rendering fidelity.

- Upload defaults are 5 MiB single / 20 MiB batch for the whole multipart body, including overhead. Direct Server uploads have no HTTP limit; UI maxSize checks an individual file. The Client supplies the multipart boundary.
- Upload failures use the standard `/api` error body with domain `file`; branch on `error.reason` (`ApiClientError.reason` in the Client), never on `message`. A successful upload answers 201.
- BODY_TOO_LARGE (413) and UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE (415): reduce request size or adjust route limits; send `multipart/form-data`. INVALID_MULTIPART/INVALID_FILE/INVALID_FILES (400): send native File values and a nonempty batch. PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED (403): a Policy function needs a resolved principal.
- INVALID_FILE_COLLECTION: first compare the migration name, route collection and Server repository argument; then await collections.get(logicalName) and check the active connection and generated metadata. SQLite physical text does not imply a broken datetime definition. Fix the specific lookup, metadata or schema problem and retry the same upload; do not bypass File Repository. Use a new migration for corrections to already-merged history.
- STORAGE_URL_UNAVAILABLE (503): configure a capable disk or stream mode.
- FILE_COMMIT_UNCERTAIN / FILE_CLEANUP_FAILED: reconcile database records and stored objects before retrying; uploads have no idempotency key.

There is no built-in route authentication, row ACL, Range/206, ETag, conditional download, resumable upload, physical cleanup, content sniffing or malware scan. Metadata deletion retains objects; cancelled forms may leave unlinked files. Implement the policies required by the business, including referenced-file deletion and orphan cleanup.

evidence.excerpt:
`policy` is required and governs every action of the exposure, uploads included. It is a Repository Policy: `read`, `create`, `update` and `delete`, each `true`, `false`, or a rule node. A node that is `false` refuses that operation; a node with no `fields` accepts no caller-supplied field, which is what a metadata `createOne` needs before it will accept anything. Pass a function of the principal — `policy: (principal) => ({ ... })` — together with a `principal(context)` resolver to scope rows to the caller; without a principal the request is refused with 403.

An upload supplies no caller fields, so it binds a Policy derived from this one: the `create` scope and defaults are inherited and the field allowlist is replaced by the file columns. `create: false` therefore forbids uploading as well as creating metadata — decided, with the principal, before the body limit, the content type or the multipart body is read, so a refused upload answers `403 WRITE_FORBIDDEN` (domain `app`) and stores nothing — and a `create.defaults` of `{ ownerId }` is stamped onto uploaded rows — which is what keeps an uploaded file inside the same scope `findMany` reads. The content route under `accessPath` is the exception: it is public and this Policy does not reach it.

Content is GET `<accessPath>/<uuid>.<ext>` outside `/api`, omitting the dot when extensionless. Stream returns full bytes as an attachment; redirect returns a public storage URL or a five-minute signed URL. A disk without URL support requires stream mode; there is no automatic fallback.

These are public routes. For restricted files, register App-owned authentication and authorization on the paths each contribution owns before mounting it — `/<name>/<action>` per exposed API action, `<accessPath>/*` for content. Never `router.use('*', ...)` in a contribution router: contributions share the mounted router, so it also guards the SPA and every contribution mounted after yours. Check the operation and record/parent-record access; a login page, private disk, Client filter or Policy field allowlist is not authentication. Add scoped middleware and principal-based Policy to the generated routes first. If an existing contract needs an adapter, extend that module using the public Server manager and retain its authorization checks; missing built-in authentication alone is not a reason to replace the routes. Never trust browser-supplied ownership.
